articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is here at last, and gamers around the world can finally play after it launched Thursday. So far, the game, which takes up a whopping 212GB on your PlayStation5 or Xbox, is receiving rave reviews . GTA 6 is streaming all over Twitch, and the memes, clips and hot takes have been pouring in. articles.title: Russian missiles hit Poland as Moscow unleashes a massive attack on Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired (Handout) Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of "provocation" after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country. Russia's Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to Kyiv's strikes on Moscow's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China's Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow's largest of the nearly five-year war, denouncing what he said was Russian "terror". Zelensky, who met allies in Berlin Thursday, said Putin's attempts to "redraw the world" with Xi and Trump had been a "failure". In China, Putin said he "shared responsibility" for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a "declaration toward peace" that made no mention of Moscow's invasion of Ukraine. AFP journalists saw people hunkered down in Kyiv's metro stations, which double as overnight air-raid shelters, sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents. Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, took her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment. "It's painful to have to stop our child from living," she told AFP. Two people were killed in Lviv, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said. Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired. Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city. France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying "Russia will have to answer for its actions there". - Poland decries 'provocation' - In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations. Warsaw said no-one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the weapons flying into Poland were deliberate. "The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland," Tusk told a televised press conference in Warsaw. Thousands of European troops are taking part in military exercises in southeastern Poland. "Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence," Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO "straight away". Tusk said that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte would be in Warsaw on Saturday and that he would inform him of the incident. Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it at future US-led talks on Ukraine. - Bridge retaliation - Russia, which has refused a ceasefire, has increased its strikes as temperatures dip in Ukraine, with many fearing this winter could be the worst of the war yet. Kyiv's state energy operator reported "significant damage" to the country's energy infrastructure that had "seriously impacted the operation of the power grid". The Black Sea port city of Odesa was in a "critical" situation with a "widespread power outage", it said -- adding blackouts were also recorded in Kyiv and 10 other regions. Russia's military on Friday confirmed it had launched a "massive" attack with missiles and drones, saying they targeted military-industrial sites and transport infrastructure in several regions, including bridges in Kyiv. The UN has reported rising civilian casualties this year as Russia intensifies its long-range strikes. UNICEF on Friday said at least 114 children had been killed and 1,030 wounded in the first 10 months of 2026 -- "a higher number of verified child casualties than in any of the past three years". "That is on average of more than three children killed or injured every single day," the organisation said, warning of an "alarming escalation in violence affecting children in Ukraine". US-led talks on ending the fighting have so far shown little signs of progress, with Moscow having stuck to its hardline demands. Putin has said a deal to end the war in Ukraine must be part of a wider agreement on European security. Speaking in China on Thursday, he said any form of Ukraine-Europe military cooperation as part of that deal would be a "problem". bur-oc/jc/phz This article originally appeared on AFP at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/russia-pummels-ukraine-putin-vowed-073406181.html

articles.title: NSA employees return to work after nearly 4 days locked out of classified network
articles.summary: This June 6, 2013, file photo, shows a sign outside the National Security Agency campus in Fort Meade, Maryland. - Patrick Semansky/AP/File The outage of a key internal communications network at the National Security Agency that has kept large swaths of employees locked out for more than three days has now been resolved, according to a source familiar with the matter and a voicemail inbox recording for employees at the main headquarters in Maryland. Employees have been told to return to work on staggered arrivals to avoid overloading the system with too many simultaneous logons, according to the source, but the expectation is that the majority of staff will be back to work by midday on Friday. “November 20, 2026, NSA Washington is operating under normal conditions with exceptions,” the voicemail said, detailing the staggering arrivals. “Personnel must follow their designating building opening times.” Several officials emphasized that the agency’s most sensitive and important intelligence gathering systems functioned throughout the outage. And although the outage froze employees out of what essentially functions as the NSA’s classified email system, the agency has multiple backups and workarounds it can use. But patches necessary to resolve the outage took longer than anticipated, a senior administration official acknowledged yesterday. On several occasions over the past several days, some employees were told to report to work on a staggered basis, only have to return home without ever logging in, according to another source familiar with the agency’s response. The system, known as NSANet, has experienced outages before. But the length of the outage — almost four days — was unusually long and disruptive, current and former officials said. Multiple current US officials briefed on this week’s outage said it was not a cyberattack but instead appeared connected to the NSA’s handling of software updates for vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language that powers about 70% of the world’s websites. Private researchers last month disclosed the vulnerabilities, which AI tools helped discover. The NSA itself urged organizations to apply software patches. articles.title: FEMA has an emergency of its own as bed bugs force workers out of headquarters
articles.summary: Employees at the Federal Emergency Management Agenc y’s Washington, D.C., headquarters have reportedly been ordered to stay home due to a bed bug infestation. More than 1,000 staffers were forced to work from home while some of the agency’s offices were fumigated Thursday and received a warning Wednesday night not to come in, The Washington Post and CNN report. The infestation was found across multiple floors of the agency’s offices in the 500 C Street building. It tops off a turbulent week for the Department of Homeland Security , which oversees FEMA, following the potential cybersecurity concerns of last week’s air traffic control outage. “This closure is necessary to perform a comprehensive, building-wide pest control treatment to address an active pest issue and ensure a safe, healthy workspace for all personnel,” an internal memo to employees reportedly said, adding that staff would be updated once the situation had been “successfully resolved.” Employees at the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Washington, DC, site have reportedly been ordered to stay home due to a bed bug infestation (AFP/Getty) The Independent has contacted FEMA for comment. Staff expressed frustration after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin mobilized the agency after the nationwide ground stop on November 13. FEMA was instructed to coordinate with airports to help get medication and other supplies to stranded passengers across the country, but after 24 hours, the assignment ended. Staffers were reportedly “mostly sat around” with little to do. “It was a giant waste of time and resources,” a FEMA official told CNN. “Pull people from their actual important work to pretend they are doing work... and [potentially] infect them with bed bugs while doing it,” another staffer complained to the Post . Bed bug infestations can lead to people facing bites on their skin and unsanitary stains on their linens, plus time-consuming and costly efforts to find and eradicate the bugs. Bed bug infestations can lead to people facing bites on their skin and unsanitary stains on their linens (AFP via Getty Images) FEMA’s reported infestation is not the first time a federal building has been plagued with bed bugs, which are notoriously difficult to eliminate. In June, employees at the U.S. Department of Agriculture - ironically, the agency charged with protecting the country against invasive pests - were sent home after the offices were repeatedly infested with bed bugs. Employees reporting to the George Washington Carver Center in Beltsville, Maryland, were warned of the infestation in mid-May. The irony of the outbreak happening in the offices of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service “was lost on no one,” a USDA employee told NOTUS at the time. articles.title: How Jensen Huang reportedly made humiliation routine at Nvidia
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang interacts with a Disney animatronic robot during his keynote address at the company's annual GTC developers conference at the SAP Center in San Jose, California, on March 16, 2026. (Photo by JOSH EDELSON / AFP via Getty Images) Earlier this week at the DealBook conference in New York, Elon Musk, beamed in from a trip to China with President Donald Trump, was asked about the ouster of his longtime friend, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Musk compared it to kicking Michael Jordan off the Chicago Bulls’ roster during his historic run. Of Nvidia’s employees, he said, “They love [Huang]. They love him.” Well, maybe not all of them. Thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for Huang’s return, but others tell The New York Times he ruled through praise and fear, and also by humiliating people. According to the Times, Huang told subordinates that Nvidia’s wealth meant it wasn’t possible to motivate them with money, so humiliation was the only lever left. He reportedly told one executive his mother should have aborted him, and told another employee he would rip his arms off and beat him to death with them. Naturally, over a 33-year career, regrettable things may have been said, but the Times found a long paper trail that suggests the incidents weren’t isolated. In 2005, for example, Michael Winston, a former HR chief, threatened to sue and called Huang’s conduct the most abusive he’d seen. Nvidia paid him more than $1 million. Huang’s spokesman calls the allegations fabrications. This article originally appeared on TechCrunch at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/behind-jensen-huang-exit-questions-132500300.html

articles.title: GOP leaders criticize members who are no-shows in Washington after losing re-election
articles.summary: Speaker of the House Mike Johnson, talks with reporters in the US Capitol on Thursday, November 19. - Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc/Getty Images In one of Republicans’ final weeks in power, GOP leaders couldn’t convince enough of their members to come back to Washington to actually vote on their own bills — and Rep. Greg Murphy was furious. Murphy, who just lost his eastern North Carolina seat in one of the biggest upsets of the midterms, unleashed on his GOP colleagues in a closed-door meeting Wednesday, urging leadership to cut off pay for any lawmakers who don’t show up, according to multiple people in the room. “Look, I lost. I’m still here. I’m still here,” Murphy later told CNN about his frustrations at some of his colleagues’ delinquency. “If they aren’t here, they shouldn’t get paid.” After their historic midterm rout, Republicans are increasingly exasperated at their otherwise-healthy GOP colleagues who are refusing to come back to Washington after their election defeats. Speaker Mike Johnson and his GOP leadership team have been privately reprimanding those who chose not to come back, including one member who told the speaker they did not return because they were worried about a CNN report of the prospect of an Iranian “dirty bomb” plot in Washington. (Johnson, when learning of the reason for the member’s absence, reminded the member that their staff was in Washington working, according to a person familiar with the discussions.) “Attendance is a great frustration for me right now,” Johnson said Thursday. “We had 14 absences yesterday, so it’s not possible for us to advance a rule and advance our legislative agenda unless the members are here doing their job. … We want to run through the tape and finish strong, but we can’t do that unless people are present at work.” It’s a glaring — and familiar — problem for Hill GOP leaders, who struggled all year trying to keep a record-small majority in line. And it comes as Republicans were already struggling with how to achieve as much of President Donald Trump’s agenda as possible before being pushed deep into the minority in January. Republican leaders are under pressure to replenish Pentagon funding after months of war with Iran, but they don’t have the votes. They want to use their GOP trifecta to raise the debt limit to avoid a Democratic showdown with Trump next year. And they want to accomplish big legacy items, like permitting reform, before they’re forced to start over with Democrats in charge. House Republicans believe the best way to accomplish Trump’s wants — particularly on the debt limit and Pentagon funding for the war — is by sidestepping Democrats altogether and doing a party-line bill. But any party-line bill is logistically challenging in the Senate, where Majority Leader John Thune has put a pause on his party’s push to take that route. Now, Hill Republicans are increasingly worried they could squander their final days in power, with absences further complicating an already-difficult December puzzle. Some in GOP leadership privately fear that the only things Republicans will accomplish in December is punting government funding into the new year – maybe paired with an extension of the nation’s expired spy powers, according to multiple people familiar with the discussions. They also worry about political theatre that could distract from the agenda, with GOP Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, a frequent leadership antagonist, forcing votes on the Epstein files and ending the Iran war. Already, there’s some talk of sending the House home after passing a stopgap bill ahead of the December 11 funding deadline – and canceling the following weeks’ worth of scheduled votes – because Republicans won’t have the votes to do more, according to several of those people. “There’s a possibility we can squander it if we don’t get our members back here,” senior GOP Rep. Mike Simpson said about the remaining days of Republican control. “What do we do to these guys that won’t come back?” Rep. Jim Jordan, the incoming House GOP minority leader, is among the Republicans pushing to use that party-line process — known as reconciliation — to get Trump priorities done before the Democratic takeover. “I’m in favor of getting as much done as we possibly can,” Jordan told CNN when asked about his preference for a GOP-only bill, adding he wants to see “all kinds of important things, like debt ceiling issue, like the defense issue.” Asked whether that would include funding for Iran, Jordan added: “That’s certainly important.” Thune, for his part, said Thursday that they likely won’t move ahead on a party-line bill until after Thanksgiving — when both chambers will have just three work weeks left. Many Republicans see it as a tacit acknowledgement that the party won’t get anything substantive done before handing over the gavels. In the Senate, Republicans are squarely focused on confirming more Trump judges, landing a long-awaited permitting reform bill and finding a way to get money for the Pentagon. Sen. John Hoeven of North Dakota said he and others are still hoping Democrats will be willing to help pass some of that Pentagon funding — even as an emboldened Senate Democratic caucus makes clear that it won’t approve more money for the Iran war. “They can vote against the military and tell everybody why they’re doing it,” Hoeven said of Democrats. “We’re trying to give them an opportunity to join us and do the right thing, which is vote support our military.” If that doesn’t work, Hoeven acknowledged Republicans will need to try again on the party-line reconciliation push despite its difficulty. But GOP Sen. John Cornyn of Texas was blunt about the prospects for that bill: “Everybody recognizes this is going to be a Herculean effort trying to get the House and the Senate to agree on the scope and the process.” And Murphy, the North Carolina Republican chiding his colleagues for their absences, added this: “It’ll be hard if people don’t show up to their job.” CNN’s Morgan Rimmer, Ted Barrett, Aileen Graef, Manu Raju and Logan Schiciano contributed to this report. articles.title: ICE spent $1 billion on detention warehouses. Now it's selling most of them.
articles.summary: ( NewsNation ) — ICE spent more than $1 billion on warehouses it now plans mostly to sell, and a federal watchdog says the agency failed to properly check whether those purchases made financial sense. The Government Accountability Office report , published Thursday, looked at how Immigration and Customs Enforcement is using the $45 billion Congress made available for detention under a 2025 law. That money runs through fiscal year 2029 and has not all been spent. Between January and March 2026, ICE bought 11 warehouses for about $1.07 billion to turn into detention and processing sites . Those plans were scaled back, and seven of the buildings are now up for sale. ICE also paid about $2.2 billion for four existing detention facilities. GOA said the agency did not update its spending plan as those plans changed or examine the long-term costs. articles.title: Mamdani sets plan to close NYC's notorious Rikers Island jail and build new jails
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — New York City's Rikers Island jail complex would close by 2032 under a sweeping plan announced Friday by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose strategy for finally shuttering the notorious facility hinges on substantially reducing the number of people kept behind bars. The mayor, a Democrat, unveiled the plan as the city is all but certain to blow past a legal requirement to close Rikers and replace it with four smaller, more modern jails by 2027. For years, Rikers Island has stood as a symbol of dysfunction, with the network of jails so plagued by violence and overcrowding that a federal judge, citing “ abnormal and unacceptable ” conditions, appointed an outside manager to restore order and implement reforms. Mamdani has been a vocal proponent of closing Rikers, though the longstanding plan to build new jails has met fierce pushback, including from his predecessor, former Mayor Eric Adams, who opposed federal oversight and borough jails. At a celebratory news conference at City Hall, Mamdani said the extended timeline was needed because of resistance from the previous administration, calling Rikers “a place we have long turned our eyes away from rather than confront head on.” “The call to close Rikers has echoed across our city for decades. Work has begun to do so, then stopped, then started once again. What will make this chapter different is our commitment to see it through,” he said. The plan centers on a goal of lowering the city's inmate population from the around 6,700 people currently housed at Rikers to a little over 4,000. The Mamdani administration is proposing a new slate of diversion and supervised release programs, expanding housing and social services to prevent recidivism, along with restoring an online bail payment system and reducing case delays so people spend less time behind bars. “Our nation has a very real mass incarceration problem,” the mayor said. “We are making a conscious decision to advance a new model of a criminal legal system in our city, one that takes on that problem head on.” Instead of housing prisoners at Rikers — an island in the East River near LaGuardia Airport — the city will shift people to jails in the Bronx, Queens, Brooklyn and Manhattan, as well as a handful of medical facilities for people who need healthcare or psychiatric treatment. The city also plans to reduce the number of beds for women, diverting them into community-based programs. The borough jails are expected to open in Brooklyn in 2029; the Bronx and Queens in 2031; and then Manhattan in 2032, according to City Hall. The new deadlines require approval from the New York City Council. Julie Menin, speaker of the City Council, praised the mayor’s plan at the news conference, saying that after years of delay “we are finally getting back on track.” The City Council voted to close the jail complex in 2019 and replace it with newer jails located in the city's boroughs by 2027. At the time, city officials had also called for shrinking the jail population to accommodate the closure, but ran into opposition from critics who argued doing so would mean more violent criminals on city streets. articles.title: Iowans say warning Army is going to blow up degraded lead came too late
articles.summary: Eight months after discovering a cache of highly reactive lead waste at an ammunitions plant in southeastern Iowa, the U.S. Army plans to do what it says is the only safe option: blow up the barrels. The controlled detonation of degraded lead azide was originally planned for Friday but was pushed to Monday after an outcry from residents and officials, who said they had not been given sufficient warning or input. Though the operation had been in the works for months, it wasn’t until Sunday that the Army notified the public about a resulting plume of lead particles that could extend as far as 100 miles north of the plant. In a Thursday night post on X announcing the delay, acting secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the three-day delay was the latest the explosion could be postponed before a forecasted cold snap, which would further destabilize the sensitive material. Get Climate Coach newsletter News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free Shortly afterward, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) posted that the delay would allow the Army to “further educate the public.” But the extra time may not be enough to allay fears of lead contamination in a state where many are already on edge about the nation’s fast-rising cancer rate and potential health effects from pesticide use . Lead is a potent neurotoxin that can cause developmental problems and other health harms if it is inhaled or swallowed, according to the Environmental Protection Agency. Infants, children and pregnant women are especially vulnerable, and science has not established any safe level of exposure . “I understand that it is confusing and obviously this is not something that we wanted to do,” said Army spokeswoman Justine Barati. “But this is a emergent hazard that has to be addressed.” The degraded lead azide, an explosive used in munitions, has become so unstable it has to be destroyed, she said. Officials plan to detonate 68 barrels of the material inside the underground concrete chambers where they have been stored for 20 years. The buried chambers will be covered in two-stories worth of sand and sprayed down with misters in an effort to limit the amount of lead that is released. In an assessment released Wednesday, the Army concluded these measures will ensure the operation has a “less-than-significant impact” on the environment and public health. The Army posted an advisory this week instructing people to stay indoors with windows closed while the lead is airborne, and to wipe down surfaces that children might touch after the all-clear has been given. In Middletown, a 363-person town immediately next to the plant, some residents were told to evacuate in case the explosion causes windows to shatter. Yet many Iowans felt the communications around the detonation were too vague and came far too late. Even Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds (R) found out about the operation from a public advisory just four days before the Army originally scheduled the operation, a spokesperson said. “It feels very rushed and very short term,” said one nearby resident, who spoke on the condition of anonymity for fear of backlash and because her relative works for the plant. “We’re all like, ‘Okay you’re saying this, but is it true, or how much of it is true?’” After learning the operation had been postponed, she said it was a “great sign” the Army was listening to residents’ concerns. Yet she and her family plan to leave the area on Monday, and she remains worried about what they will return to. Will her garden be contaminated? Will food grown in the surrounding farmland be safe to eat? Environmental groups on Thursday filed a lawsuit seeking an emergency stay of the detonation and a court review of the EPA’s decision to issue a permit. Several Iowa officials, including Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) and U.S. Sen.-elect Josh Turek (D) also called on the Army to delay the operation until residents’ fears could be addressed. Representatives for Sand, Turek and the groups behind the lawsuit did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the Army’s decision to postpone. Under the terms of the EPA emergency permit , the Iowa Army Ammunitions Plant was required to map where airborne lead concentrations could reach 18 micrograms per cubic meter — a threshold below the federal exposure limit for workplace air. A second required map showed where the plume could deposit lead dust at concentrations of 5 micrograms per square foot (which the EPA considers a hazardous level of lead on floors ) and 100 micrograms per square foot (the hazardous level for window troughs ). These maps , released Sunday, showed that surface deposition of lead could extend 30 miles north, reaching the Mississippi River and parts of Illinois. Neither the Army nor the EPA responded to questions about what the maximum concentrations of lead in the plume are expected to be. Officials first became aware there was a problem during a regular inspection of the lead azide barrels at the plant this spring, Barati said. The liquid used to stabilize the material had dried out, and the lead azide began to form crystals — a condition that makes it much more likely to spontaneously explode. The Army is still trying to determine what caused the substance to recrystallize, Barati said. Just one minute of this activity may cut blood sugar spikes by 40 percent At historic summit, Xi and Putin share global stage with weakened Trump The 41 definitive rules of hosting A team of experts then spent the next several months trying to figure out what to do about it. Chemical neutralization would involve opening the barrels, potentially disturbing the crystals and creating “an extreme and unacceptable risk of fatal accidental detonation,” according to an Army assessment . Moving the barrels, either to an uninhabited area or even a more remote part of the facility, carried the same danger. If they did nothing, the lead azide would be a ticking time bomb — one that cold weather could make even more dangerous. By September, the Army concluded that a controlled detonation was the only viable option. The Army informed Middletown emergency services officials in September and held an open house for the town’s residents the following month, according to Barati. Communities beyond Middletown were not initially told about the operation because the lead levels they might be exposed to were thought to be “minuscule,” she said. But the EPA emergency permit, which was issued Nov. 13, required five day’s notice for anyone living within the plume, so the Army began reaching out to city councils, fire departments and other local officials, she said. By Monday, the news began trickling out on social media, raising alarm bells across the state. “When we first found out about it we thought it was fake,” said Cody Smith, a program manager for the Iowa Environmental Council. He said that local officials he spoke to had received no guidance from the Army or EPA on ways to protect their residents, and many were making decisions on the fly about whether to close schools and other facilities. The incident also raises questions about whether communities are safe from other hazards connected to the plant, Smith added. “Having not discovered this until earlier in the year is deeply concerning and speaks to a level of negligence from the Army itself,” he said. Barati said the Iowa plant was permitted to store lead azide and conducted inspections every six months to ensure it was safe. Some of the residents’ fear traces back to past concerns about the World War II-era facility, said Susan Dahl Mattoon, who grew up in the area and still works at Southeastern Community College in nearby Burlington. She recalled hearing the “booms” from ordnance tests and wondering what might be happening behind its gates. The plant was named a Superfund site in 1990 due to widespread soil and water contamination. About 10 years later, dozens of employees were found to have developed cancers likely related to their work on a nuclear weapons assembly line there. “Honestly our plant out here has had a reputation for looking the other way in the past,” Mattoon said. That’s why the short notice and lack of detail about effects has her so concerned, she said. David Cwiertny, director of the Center for Health Effects of Environmental Contamination at the University of Iowa, said it’s difficult to independently evaluate the possible risks from the detonation without additional information. The permit does not explain what models the Army used to forecast the potential lead dispersion or how they determined that the impact would be “less than significant.” The Army’s guidance for residents is also confusing, he said. If the level of lead in the plume is insignificant, why advise people to avoid the area and wipe down playground equipment afterward, he asked. If lead deposited on a slide is unsafe, why is it any better to wash it onto the ground where children might also be playing? Whether or not the detonation presents a major threat, the official messaging around it falls short of the central tenets of public health messaging, Cwiertny said. “Better engagement, better and clearer communication, focusing on what real public health risks are, explaining expertise and assumptions used to arrive at those conclusions — all of that is needed, else people are just going to fill in the blank with their own thoughts and frustrations,” he said. articles.title: 花旗低估欧洲交易部门风险资产约350亿美元，称已完成整改
articles.summary: 花旗集团在欧洲一家交易子公司的内部资本建模问题上出现重大失误，低估风险加权资产约350亿美元，再度引发外界对这家华尔街大行合规管控能力的关注。 据路透社报道，花旗今年早些时候在上述欧洲交易部门低估了风险加权资产规模。花旗集团随后确认，该问题已于今夏被识别并解决。 花旗集团表示，"该子公司在整个过程中始终符合监管最低资本要求，对母公司或主要运营银行均无影响"，并称已完成整改措施并注入资本，以立即恢复该子公司的资本缓冲。 然而，这一事件发生在花旗仍面临监管压力的背景之下，或进一步复杂化其与监管机构之间的关系。 截至发稿，周五盘中花旗下跌1.6%。 建模问题源于未经监管批准的内部模型 据路透社援引知情人士称，花旗在其英国证券部门使用了一套基于自身统计假设的内部模型来记录交易，而该模型并未获得监管机构批准，由此导致风险加权资产被低估约350亿美元。 风险加权资产是银行资本充足率计算的核心指标，低估该数值将使银行对外呈现出高于实际水平的资本充足率，从而在监管层面形成虚假的安全边际。 花旗表示，问题发现后已迅速注资修复资本缓冲，子公司资本水平在此期间始终满足监管最低要求。 合规整改进程再添变数 这一事件令花旗的监管整改进程再度承压。花旗集团首席执行官Jane Fraser多年来持续推动解决该行合规问题，但监管审视从未真正消散。 花旗目前仍在努力解决2020年由货币监理署（OCC）和美联储联合下达的两项同意令。这两项监管令因花旗内部控制及后台系统存在缺陷而设立，至今仍未解除。 据路透社报道，花旗最近一次寻求进展是在今夏，该行正争取在年底前向监管机构提交相关文件，以推动上述限制措施的解除。此次欧洲子公司的建模失误，无疑为这一进程增添了新的不确定性。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: Anthropic上市次日暴跌，几乎回吐首日涨幅，AI交易“买方罢工”
articles.summary: 史上最大IPO的光环正在消退。Anthropic上市第二日股价急剧下滑，几乎抹去首日涨幅，映射出更广泛AI与科技板块的抛售情绪，同时也为竞争对手OpenAI的未来上市之路埋下变数。 Anthropic股价周五盘中一度跌至87.26美元，距83美元的发行价仅剩5.1%的涨幅，而该股在上市首日曾短暂将公司市值推升至高于亚马逊。 与此同时，承销银行行使超额配售权（绿鞋机制），进一步扩大股票供给，使Anthropic此次IPO及联合私募合计融资规模升至1195亿美元。 市场大环境同样构成压力。周五，抛售浪潮从亚洲蔓延至美国，纳斯达克100指数下跌1.5%，标普500指数跌0.5%，芝加哥期权交易所波动率指数（VIX）飙升至29以上——远超企业通常视为市场欢迎IPO的水位线。 Anthropic此次上市的战略意义超出单一公司范畴。作为首家上市的前沿AI模型开发商，其市场表现实质上是对投资者能否为AI底层技术本身（而非芯片、数据中心等基础设施）定价买单的一次直接测试。 买盘观望，AI热度遭遇"买方罢工" Forte Securities的Emmanuel Valavanis将当前局面描述为"针对Anthropic乃至整个AI和科技交易的买方罢工"。 他指出，许多客户在此次IPO配售中未能获得份额，在未持有仓位、也无指数跟踪压力的情况下，这部分投资者宁愿在场外等待更长期的价格发现，也不愿贸然接盘。 这一动态揭示出IPO首日溢价背后的脆弱性：当核心买家已在发行价锁定筹码，二级市场缺乏增量资金入场时，股价承压几乎是必然结果。 对于投资者而言，当前市场波动加剧了观望情绪。 Vega IS基金经理Olivier David表示，若股价接近甚至跌破发行价，其团队将考虑在公开市场买入。 历史性IPO：融资规模与市场地位 此次上市创下多项纪录。Anthropic成为史上最大规模IPO的主角，同时也是首家登陆美股的前沿AI模型开发商，超越了SpaceX今年6月创下的866亿美元纪录。 在承销层面，高盛、摩根士丹利及另外20家银行共计获得5.5亿美元费用，同样刷新历史纪录。 IPO及联合私募合计融资中，IPO部分为935亿美元，私募部分为260亿美元。按当前股价计算，Anthropic市值约为1.5万亿美元，位列全球上市公司前15位。公司七位联合创始人的合计财富升至1660亿美元。 包括Anthropic在内，美国市场今年首次公开募股总规模已达2580亿美元，超越2021年1950亿美元的历史高点（均剔除特殊目的收购公司等金融工具）。 基本面支撑：企业客户驱动营收高速增长 股价波动之外，Anthropic的基本面数据提供了部分支撑。 根据监管文件，截至10月31日，公司年化运营收入达810亿美元，较9月底增加100亿美元。截至9月底，年度贡献收入超过10万美元的企业客户数量超过11900家，而2025年初这一数字仅约为1500家。 公司旗下面向软件开发者的编程代理产品Claude Code在业内获得广泛应用，监管文件显示其用户甚至涵盖NASA工程师。Anthropic以专注企业客户为核心策略，这一路径赢得了部分机构投资者的认可。 Tikehau Capital资本市场策略主管Raphael Thuin对此评价称，"这家公司在短短数年内创造的财富令人印象深刻，自由现金流消耗也相对合理"，但同时表示， 其团队在AI领域更倾向于布局多元化业务，且希望等待IPO后的波动性消退后再考虑进一步介入。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美国11月密歇根大学消费者信心指数回升，通胀预期大幅下降
articles.summary: 美国消费者信心在11月出现反弹，主要受汽油价格下降、商业环境预期改善及通胀预期骤降等因素推动，表明选后政策预期的转变正在影响家庭情绪。 密歇根大学周五公布的数据显示， 该校消费者信心指数11月终值升至51.5，高于10月的48。彭博调查经济学家的预测中值为51.6，实际数据与之基本吻合。 调查结果显示， 消费者对未来一年的通胀预期从10月的4.7%骤降至3.7%，创2月以来最低；未来5至10年的长期通胀预期亦有所回落。与此同时，反映个人当前财务状况的分项指数升至7月以来最高水平。 汽油价格下跌是本月消费者情绪改善的重要支撑之一。 据美国汽车协会（AAA）数据，全国每加仑汽油均价在11月初仍高于4美元，但在密歇根大学调查结束时已回落至约3.75美元。 选举结果提振预期，独立选民情绪明显改善 密歇根大学本轮调查于10月20日至11月16日期间进行，涵盖了美国中期选举的投票结果公布阶段。 此次选举中，民主党在众议院、参议院均获胜，并在乔治亚州、爱荷华州、德克萨斯州、俄亥俄州及内华达州赢得州长职位。 调查负责人Joanne Hsu在声明中表示，消费者似乎已开始预判分裂政府格局下公共政策可能发生的变化，预期指数在独立选民中出现显著跳升。 她还指出， 选举结束后消费者对汽油价格的预期大幅下滑，目前已"基本回落至伊朗问题发酵前的水平"。 高通胀与高利率仍是压制因素 尽管信心指数有所回升，美国家庭面临的整体经济压力并未根本缓解。经济学家估计，10月消费者价格指数同比涨幅仍约为4%；自9月中旬以来，30年期抵押贷款利率持续高于7%，借贷成本依然高企。 持续攀升的物价此前已将消费者信心压至历史极端水平——5月触及历史最低，10月录得有记录以来第二低位。 经济状况与生活成本是此次中期选举的核心议题，食品、汽油、医疗及住房价格高涨引发的选民不满情绪，也在一定程度上影响了选举结果走向。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 市场热议的DeepSeek第二轮融资终于落定。上海证券报记者梳理发现，至少已有9家券商通过不同路径入局新一轮融资，经测算对应出资总额约95.20亿元。 9家券商入局 工商信息显示，DeepSeek核心运营主体杭州深度求索人工智能基础技术研究有限公司已于近日完成工商变更，新增股东杭州程砚企业管理咨询合伙企业（有限合伙）（下称“杭州程砚”），公司注册资本增至1991.8707万元，增幅约21%。作为本轮外部融资的统一持股平台，杭州程砚同步完成工商变更：新增31家合伙人，登记出资额由0.6万元增至34.39亿元。 企查查数据显示，DeepSeek本轮融资规模约1055亿元，投后估值约6155亿元。其中，至少已有9家券商参投DeepSeek，分别为中信证券、中金公司、国元证券、财通证券、东方证券、浙商证券、申万宏源、华福证券、中信建投。 从参与方式来看，券商的布局路径各有差异： 一是通过另类投资子公司开展直投业务。例如，中信证券通过全资另类子公司中信证券投资持有杭州程砚7.6522%份额，穿透持有DeepSeek约1.3212%，对应出资约80.73亿元；中金公司则通过中金浦成持有约0.4783%份额，叠加中金河钢所持0.0045%份额，合计持有杭州程砚约0.4828%份额，穿透对应出资约5.09亿元。 二是以有限合伙人（LP）身份，通过私募基金间接参与，这是目前中小券商的主流参与方式。国元证券、东方证券、浙商证券、华福证券均现身杭州石溪兆易一号的合伙人名单；财通证券通过天津砺思星深持有杭州程砚份额；申万宏源、中信建投则分别通过嘉兴聚源曜辉、福建时代泽远等基金主体间接入场。 整体来看，9家券商合计持有杭州程砚约9.0234%份额，穿透持有DeepSeek约1.5579%，对应总出资约95.20亿元。其中，中信证券单家出资占券商系总额的84%，其余8家券商合计出资不足15亿元，行业“马太效应”显著。 券商为何集体抢滩？ 券商集体抢滩明星项目的背后，是科创投资业务利润的集中释放，券商的“科创属性”已从传统的通道业务延伸至资本赋能层面。以另类子公司为例，2026年上半年，41家上市券商另类子公司合计实现净利润202.75亿元，多家公司同比增幅达数倍。 不少券商业绩贡献突出：国泰海通、招商证券、中信证券旗下另类子公司上半年净利润分别达65.07亿元、52.20亿元和19.75亿元，对母公司净利润贡献度依次为32.12%、49.13%和8.46%；华安证券旗下华富瑞兴上半年净利润5.34亿元，占公司归母净利润的25.47%。 此外，跟投也是股权投资业务重要的业绩放大器。国金证券研报数据显示，自科创板开板至今，科创板募资规模合计达1054.55亿元，其中券商科创板跟投金额合计31.34亿元，合计实现上市首日跟投收益138.52亿元。 利润的集中兑现，推动行业资源加速倾斜。2026年以来，浙商证券公告向浙商投资增资10亿元；财达证券拟出资2.5亿元在北京新设另类子公司；东吴证券、中泰证券、南京证券等均在定增方案中明确将部分募集资金投向另类投资或私募股权业务。 在国金证券非银首席分析师舒思勤看来，股权投资业务已成为重要盈利贡献因素，其竞争力将越来越不取决于短期行情，而取决于三个核心能力的建设：产业研判的前瞻性、项目筛选的精准度、投后管理与退出通道的多元性。 本文来源： 上海证券报 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 工商银行、建设银行、招商银行、宁波银行同日提示贵金属市场风险
articles.summary: 近期贵金属市场的不确定性因素较多，价格波动加剧。 11月20日晚间，招商银行发布关于近期贵金属业务市场风险提示公告，提醒投资者提高贵金属业务的风险防范意识，基于自身财务状况、风险承受能力及投资经验，理性开展贵金属投资活动，合理控制贵金属资产持仓规模，避免短期投机或跟风交易，从长期资产配置视角理性配置贵金属资产，控制投资总量，做好多元布局。 此前，工商银行、建设银行也已发布贵金属业务市场风险提示。工商银行建议投资者密切关注市场变化，提升风险防控意识，坚持适度均衡的原则，从中长期视角理性进行投资配置，守护资产安全。 建设银行也提示，请投资者在投资该行贵金属业务时，提高贵金属业务的风险防范意识，基于自身财务状况和风险承受能力理性、稳健投资，合理控制仓位，避免盲目跟风操作。同时，提醒投资者及时关注持仓情况和保证金余额变化情况，防范贵金属市场风险。 银行密集提示风险的背后，是近期国际金价的大幅回调。短短5个交易日，国际现货黄金接连跌破3900美元/盎司、3800美元/盎司、3700美元/盎司和3600美元/盎司四道关口。 11月20日，现货黄金抛压延续，日内最大跌幅逾3%，一度逼近3500美元/盎司。截至发稿，现货黄金报3571.75美元/盎司，日内跌1.53%，本周累计下跌约8%，此前已连跌4个交易日；当前点位创2025年9月以来新低，较年初历史高点回撤超2000美元，年内跌幅已超17%。 与其高度联动的积存金价随之下探进入“7字头”区间。截至发稿，工银积存金价报769元/克，当日跌幅达3.5%。 多家券商研报分析认为，近期国际金价走弱，主要受到美联储货币政策预期变化影响。随着美联储释放偏鹰派信号，市场对进一步加息的预期升温，推动美元及美债收益率走强。作为无息资产，黄金的持有机会成本随之上升，部分资金选择获利了结或转向其他资产，进一步加剧金价下跌。 中信建投证券在2027年黄金投资展望中表示，美国经济呈现分化、油价高基数将削弱能源对通胀的拉动、市场已充分定价2027年美联储加息，叠加美国财政付息压力硬性约束，预期实际利率进一步上行空间有限，金价压力有望逐步缓解。 本文来源： 上海证券报 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

Gamma 正凑在一起，市场不再是平缓的线性波动，要提妨“恐慌定价、机械对冲、流动性变薄”三者共振。 VIX 跳升 + 倒挂（Backwardation）：平时 VIX 期货大多是近低远高的升水结构（Contango），做空波动率能赚时间移仓；一旦转为倒挂，说明短端即期避险需求瞬间压过远期预期，大家在抢眼前的“防跌保单”。 做市商账面已经累积了相当规模的空头对冲敞口，市场本身就处于偏紧绷的净对冲状态（负delta），一旦波动率抬升（通常系统波动率超过28+Back），Vanna 效应会同步介入：隐含波动率一跳，Vanna效应就会先一步将原本虚值看跌期权的 Delta 绝对值拉大，做市商账面原本就负delta带来的对冲压力进一步收紧，做市商在期权端被动承担 Short Put 敞口时，为了维持中性，需要在标的资产端维持对应的对冲仓位；当虚值 Put 的 Delta 绝对值被 IV 跳升拉大时，账面的对冲需求就会同步拉紧，逼着做市商在现货或期货端追加操作。 Vanna负责在波动率跳升时先把“对冲绳索”拉紧，而负 Gamma 则在价格破位或下杀时把绳索越拉越紧：随着指数向下方行权价靠拢、负 Gamma 敞口继续扩大，做市商的机械动作就是“跌了还得继续顺势卖、涨了反而要买回平仓”，盘面缺少正 Gamma 那种“跌了自动抄底接盘”的减震器，一旦遇到外部消息或买盘断层，负 Gamma 接棒，价格越跌、对冲敞口变化越快，做市商在现货/期货端的顺势调仓就会进一步放大盘面波动，日内振幅和下杀惯性很容易被放大。 整体的逻辑就变成了：现货走弱——负 Gamma 逼着做市商顺势卖出对冲——指数进一步下探、VIX 高贝塔（信息技术、通信服务）下跌、防御与补涨板块（必需消费品、软件）上涨，板块之间互相抵消了指数层面的波动。此时指数的实际波动率与隐含相关性被压在低位。 但一旦指数被高贝塔权重拖入负 Gamma 区间并引发 VIX 抬升，就会引发 期权做市商的 Vanna 效应： 当市场下跌伴随 VIX 走高（隐含波动率扩张），客户端持有的虚值看跌期权Delta 绝对值迅速放大，处于空头一方的做市商为了维持 卖压下出现破位回勾，不仅意味着场内避风港失守，还会反过来推高指数的整体实现波动率，进一步刺激 VIX 上行，触发做市商更猛烈的二次 Vanna 抛售和 Vol-Control（波动率控制）基金的降仓。 2022年同样的逻辑线（其实美股所有的反馈细节和逻辑都一样），高切低阶段：标普 500 articles.title: 美国科技人才开始逃离？H-1B签证持续收紧，高技能员工开始另寻出路
articles.summary: 特朗普政府对移民政策的持续收紧，正将美国科技行业推向一场人才危机。 11月20日，据彭博报道， H-1B签证审批延误加剧、新规频出且充满不确定性，正迫使大批高技能外籍科技工作者放弃在美发展的计划，转而寻求他国机会。 在企业层面，IBM已宣布停止为其最大业务部门的多数职位提供签证担保，微软、Adobe等科技巨头则被禁止参与关键绿卡担保项目。 与此同时，本月中期选举结果虽对特朗普移民政策构成政治压力，但分析人士指出，新一届国会要逆转相关规则变化并非易事。 移民律师及行业团体警告，这场"静悄悄的拆解"已开始在数据层面显现： 美国2025财年发放的临时非移民签证较上年减少约26万份，今秋新增外国留学生人数估计下降15%。 美国移民律师协会监督政策顾问Kate Angustia直言："我们正在制造人才外流。" 工程师出走：从"黄金囚笼"到主动离场 来自印度的谷歌软件工程师Yash Sharma是这场人才流失的缩影。这位36岁的工程师持有H-1B签证已六年，计划下月离开旧金山前往英国，尽管彼时尚无工作在手。他向媒体表示， 美国对他而言已成为一座"黄金囚笼"——热爱这里的生活，却看不到留下来的出路。 Sharma的困境具有代表性。由于印度国籍申请人面临绿卡积压，他转而申请"杰出人才"签证，但等待数月后遭拒。过去一年半，他不敢出境，担心无法再次入境，因此错过了家庭探访、工作会议和朋友出行。最终，他获批英国"全球人才签证"，该签证提供明确的长期居留路径，令他下定决心离开。 "在我看来，法律层面不会有真正的改变，"Sharma说，"即便一切恢复原状，那个'正常'依然很糟糕。" 另一位在纽约工作的印度籍高级数据分析师Swapnil Deshpande同样感受到这种压迫感。他2018年赴美攻读硕士，在美工作近六年，如今每天醒来都觉得可能是在美国的最后一天。 "我和妻子都想买房、开始新生活，但现在我们连下个月会发生什么都不知道，"他说，"这种不确定性、压力和不可预测性，真的值得吗？" 企业重构：IBM停止担保，巨头被拒于绿卡项目之外 人才流失的压力已传导至企业决策层，多家大型科技公司正在重新评估用人策略。 据彭博获得的一份向管理层传达的文件，IBM本月通知员工，将停止为其咨询部门多数职位的外籍员工提供签证担保，受影响员工须在年底前选择调往美国以外的岗位或离职。 支付公司Flywire在本季度监管文件中披露，正考虑将部分招聘和研发工作"重新分配至已有业务的低成本司法管辖区"，以抵消H-1B签证成本上升带来的压力。该公司警告，若无法招募和留住专业人才，将拖慢自身产品研发进度；而外国留学生减少赴美，也将直接压缩流经其网络的学费支付规模。 微软、Adobe及多家IT外包公司则已被联邦当局禁止参与一项关键绿卡担保项目，原因是当局正对其相关做法展开调查。 移民律师、Holland & Hart合伙人Chris Thomas表示， 其企业客户正在评估雇用外籍员工的合规风险，部分客户担忧即便合规操作，也可能遭到调查或被禁止参与签证项目。"有些客户说，这太麻烦了，是时候开始离岸外包了，" 他说。 政策收紧：新规叠加、费用激增，系统性拆解悄然推进 特朗普政府对就业移民体系的重塑，是通过一系列行政手段逐步推进的。 去年9月，H-1B项目首先成为焦点：一项总统公告要求特定境外求职者缴纳10万美元费用；今年8月，尽管法院已就原方案发出禁令，行政当局仍另行推出针对新H-1B申请的10.3万美元费用规定。 本周，美国劳工部进一步提议收紧企业为外籍员工申请永久居留权的相关规则。 在政治层面，特朗普本月任命Stephen Miller出任白宫幕僚长，这位长期主张削减各类移民的强硬派由此获得更大权力。副总统JD Vance上月宣布对雇主绿卡担保行为展开调查，进一步加剧市场压力。 特朗普政府的立场是，工人和雇主多年来滥用移民制度，使其偏离了为美国引进高度专业化临时人才的初衷，并导致美国本土工人薪资受压。 一项由哈佛大学经济学家——曾任职于特朗普经济顾问委员会——发布的研究显示，高技能移民导致受过大学教育的美国工人薪资下降，在科学领域尤为明显。不过，报道指出，学界对移民影响薪资这一问题的研究结论不一。 人才流失：数据印证，长期代价难以估量 政策收紧的影响已开始在统计数据中显现。 据移民政策研究所对联邦签证数据的分析，2025财年（含拜登政府最后三个完整月份），美国发放的临时非移民签证较上年减少约26万份。国际教育研究所数据显示，今秋美国高校新增外国留学生人数估计下降15%。可选实习项目（OPT）——为国际学生提供临时工作授权——在2026至2027学年初参与人数下降6%，为五年来首次下滑。 Compete America执行董事Scott Corley警告，规模效应一旦瓦解，后果难以逆转。"这有点像声誉：建立需要多年，毁掉却只需一瞬，"他说。 移民律师、Vialto Law合伙人Angelo Paparelli将当前局面定性为"对就业移民体系的静悄悄拆解"。 多位律师和行业人士表示，即便部分政策变化面临法律挑战，美国"不再欢迎"的形象已在全球高技能人才群体中形成，且难以在短期内扭转。 articles.title: 中国开源模型的「最大甲方」有了
articles.summary: 互联网大厂们正在成为开源大模型的新甲方。 腾讯总裁刘炽平在三季度业绩电话会上透露，WorkBuddy已成为中国几乎所有开放权重模型的最大客户。 这可能只是一个开始。 近期，国内头部办公Agent密集调整产品策略。继腾讯WorkBuddy率先采用多模型路线后，字节跳动旗下豆包工作接连扩大第三方模型接入范围，阿里千问办公也重新向外部模型敞开大门。 从腾讯到字节、阿里，几家互联网大厂的办公Agent正在走向相似的产品路线。 随着这一趋势逐渐明朗，拥有庞大用户规模、能够持续承接工作任务的办公Agent有望成为上游模型厂商新的超级客户。 但当路线趋于一致后，大厂既要通过办公Agent争夺用户和工作入口，也要在不断增长的Token消耗中控制成本。 谁能汇集更多模型需求决定了业务规模；谁能更高效地调度这些模型，则开始影响商业化的成色。 超级买家在途 WorkBuddy能够成为中国几乎所有开放权重模型最大客户，一方面与之市场影响力有关，另一方面则是因为其较早采用多模型策略。 今年3月上线时，WorkBuddy便支持接入DeepSeek、GLM、Kimi等第三方模型，此后又持续扩大模型选择范围。 这一路线在过去一段时间里并未成为国内办公Agent的主流选择。 今年8月25日，字节跳动正式推出豆包工作。产品上线初期主要依靠自研豆包模型提供服务，并未向普通用户开放第三方模型选择；同期，阿里旗下的千问办公同样以自研模型为主。 但随着WorkBuddy持续扩大领先优势，其他大厂竞争压力突增。 10月29日，豆包工作率先向团队和企业订阅用户开放第三方模型。11月12日，又进一步扩大模型接入范围，在原有自研模型之外，新增Kimi K3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash等第三方模型。 仅4天后，千问办公也迅速跟进，一口气上线10款模型，包括自研Qwen4-Max，以及Kimi、GLM、DeepSeek、MiniMax、Step等第三方模型。 事实上，阿里对于是否开放第三方模型曾有过摇摆。 今年8月，千问办公曾短暂引入GLM、DeepSeek等外部模型，但相关模型仅上线数日便从产品端下线，模型选择重新回到以自研模型为主的状态。 时隔三个月，千问办公再次向第三方模型敞开大门。 与此前的短暂尝试不同，这一次，千问办公不仅向个人和企业标准版用户开放模型选择，还允许企业管理员根据部门、用户组及员工配置模型使用权限。 从腾讯率先采用多模型聚合，到字节扩大第三方模型接入，再到阿里重新开放模型选择，国内几家头部大厂的办公Agent最终走向了相似的产品路线。 从需求端来看，对办公Agent而言，用户最终需要的是一份报告、一张表格、一段代码，或者一项能够直接交付的工作。 不同任务对模型能力、响应速度和成本的要求并不相同。单一模型未必能够在所有场景中保持优势，通过接入多家模型，用户可以根据不同任务选择更合适的模型。 这种产品路线的收敛恰恰给上游模型厂商带来新的机会。 过去，智谱、月之暗面、MiniMax等独立模型厂商主要通过自身产品、开发者生态、API服务及企业客户扩大模型使用量。如今，拥有数百万乃至千万级日活跃用户的办公Agent也开始成为一类值得争取的大客户。 这种变化已经体现在部分模型厂商的新产品发布策略中。 今年10月初，WorkBuddy曾接入一款名为Space Bunny的匿名模型。直到10月19日MiniMax正式发布M3.1 Flash，外界才得知Space Bunny正是这款模型的早期版本。 据MiniMax披露，Space Bunny在匿名运行期间累计处理超过200万亿Token。 随着腾讯、字节、阿里相继走向多模型路线，各家能够获得的底层模型能力开始趋同，单纯增加模型选择已难以形成持续的差异化优势。 如何整合不同模型的能力、提高任务交付效率，并控制模型调用成本，开始成为更现实的竞争问题。 大客户精打细算 对于这些正在成为大模型重要客户的互联网大厂而言，模型调用规模不断扩大，也意味着需要承担更高的运行成本。 腾讯管理层日前在财报电话会上明确提出，未来将通过提高付费用户比例、增加每名付费用户的Token支出，以及推理优化、模型定制和算力效率提升等方式，逐步改善单位经济效益。 一方面，办公Agent需要通过更强的任务交付能力提高用户付费意愿，并推动使用量增长；另一方面则需要控制模型推理和任务执行成本，避免收入增长被持续扩大的资源消耗抵消。 不过，随着调用规模扩大，互联网大厂在承担更高成本的同时，也可能获得新的议价筹码。 庞大的采购规模也意味着有机会争取比公开API报价更低的价格。 一家已将旗下模型接入WorkBuddy的厂商人士向华尔街见闻·全天候科技确认：“在模型API的商业合作中，折扣率会根据客户的调用规模确定。” “企业客户可以通过渠道获得低于官网公开报价的模型API服务，实际价格存在一定的协商空间。”南方一家从事大模型API代理及销售业务的企业人士向全天候科技表示。 海外的模型厂商也采取了类似的机制。 Anthropic在官方API定价规则中明确表示，大用量客户可以根据具体情况单独协商批量折扣，企业客户还可以获得定制价格及其他商业条款。 这也可能进一步影响互联网大厂在办公Agent之间的竞争。 随着WorkBuddy、豆包工作和千问办公相继走向多模型路线，各家能够获得的底层模型供给逐渐趋同，但实际支付的采购价格未必相同。 对于拥有更大模型调用规模的平台而言，庞大的采购需求有望转化为更强的议价能力，进而获得更低的单位调用价格。 一旦这种优势形成，大厂不仅能够降低模型使用成本，也可能通过更有竞争力的产品定价和服务额度争夺用户，进一步扩大调用规模，形成正向循环。 这只是竞争的一部分。真正交付一项任务还涉及模型调用次数、Token消耗，以及执行失败后的重试成本，这也对办公Agent背后的Harness提出更高要求。 Harness作为Agent的运行框架，不仅决定如何组织这些步骤，还会影响模型调用次数、上下文管理及任务失败后的重试策略。 即使使用相同的底层模型，不同Harness也可能产生显著不同的资源消耗。 今年9月，字节Seed团队与外部研究人员发表《HarnessDev》论文，专门研究不同Harness设计对Agent任务表现及运行效率的影响。 研究人员在其中一组实验中，统一使用Gemini 3.1 Pro作为底层执行模型，让不同Harness完成相同的Terminal-Bench 2.1测试。 结果显示，由GPT-5.5构建的Harness，平均执行Token消耗约为2430万个；由Claude Opus 4.8构建的Harness，平均消耗约9430万个，相差约3.9倍。 两组实验的任务成功率分别为49.4%和52.4%。后者虽然获得了略高的成功率，但Token消耗却增加了近3倍。 这也意味着，随着未来当几家互联网大厂的办公Agent陆续接入GLM、Kimi、DeepSeek等更多第三方模型时，拥有相似的模型供给并不意味着它们能够以相同的成本完成工作。 从采购到执行，互联网大厂实际上需要算清两笔账： 一笔是向模型厂商采购模型能力的价格。随着调用规模扩大，大厂有机会通过规模采购降低单位成本； 另一笔则是完成实际工作所需要的综合成本。它不仅取决于模型报价，还与模型路由、Harness运行效率等密切相关。 这两种成本优势还可能相互强化，形成正向循环。 对于拥有更大调用规模的办公Agent而言，更有利的采购价格意味着相同预算能够支撑更多模型调用和产品试验。而持续积累的真实任务反馈，又有助于大厂优化模型路由、任务拆解和执行流程，加快Harness的迭代。 随着多模型路线逐渐收敛，几家互联网大厂的办公Agent能够获得的底层模型能力越来越接近，但采购成本、Harness效率与产品迭代速度仍可能拉开差距，此刻难言胜负。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 华为星芒发车：一路踏AI，一路铺鸿蒙
articles.summary: 2016年10月14日，华为当年第1亿部智能手机正式下线，比2015年达成这一节点提前了两个月。 坐稳1亿部手机的出货量之际，华为推出了一条全新的产品线nova，希望进一步打开年轻消费市场。 十年后，华为再次迎来一个与“1亿”有关的节点。 11月16日，第三方数据显示，华为HarmonyOS 5及以上版本累计装机量已突破1亿台。 就在鸿蒙装机规模迈过亿级门槛之际，华为再次推出了全新的手机品牌。 11月20日，华为全新子品牌OSTA星芒正式亮相，首款手机OSTA O1 Pro以鸿蒙AI和阔直板设计作为重要卖点，搭载麒麟9030S芯片，起售价达到5699元，首发优惠价为5499元。 这次，华为将星芒定位为“首款为AI而生的鸿蒙手机”，试图通过新的交互方式，让AI从辅助功能走向手机使用的中心。 与十年前不同，如今中国智能手机市场的季度出货量已经几乎减半，存量竞争日趋激烈，手机厂商越来越难以依靠硬件升级刺激消费者换机。 但AI的兴起正在为智能手机行业带来新的技术变革。 对华为而言，星芒的推出不仅是争夺更多手机消费者的一次尝试，还有望借助AI带来的新机会进一步扩大鸿蒙操作系统的用户基础和和生态规模。 十年后的再孵化 nova诞生之际，正值移动互联网热潮，智能手机尚处于普及期。 这一热潮下，华为推出了子品牌nova。 但如今的手机市场早已不是十年前的模样。 IDC数据显示，2016年第三季度，中国智能手机市场出货量达到1.151亿部，同比增长5.8%；到了2026年同期，这一数字已经降至约5790万部，同比下降15.4%。 十年间，中国智能手机季度出货量几乎减半。 随着智能手机普及率趋于饱和，消费者换机周期延长，手机厂商的竞争也从争夺新增用户，逐渐转向存量市场的份额争夺。 与此同时，存储等核心零部件价格上涨，进一步加剧了手机厂商的经营压力。IDC指出，今年第三季度，中国手机市场呈现出明显的“量跌价升”现象，终端价格上涨正在抑制消费者的换机需求。 这也意味着，十年前华为能够通过nova拓展年轻消费市场、分享行业增长红利；十年后，星芒想要获得新的销量，需要有更多元化的打法。 对于此次推出新品牌的考虑，华为表示：“麒麟芯片与鸿蒙生态均已就绪，母品牌加速回归全盛，为打造全新子品牌奠定坚实基础；同时，华为渴望搭建与先锋者对话的新阵地，让品牌叙事与先锋群体同频共振。部分前沿创新技术需要前瞻式下放，子品牌正是其提前搭载、率先释放的最佳载体。” 此次首款OSTA O1 Pro采用16:9.5比例的阔直板设计，配备6.39英寸1.5K屏幕，搭载麒麟9030S芯片，机身厚度仅6.68毫米，重量约200克。 影像方面，新机配备2亿像素RYYB主摄、5000万像素潜望式长焦及红枫镜头；续航方面则搭载7000mAh电池，支持66W有线充电和无线充电。 不过，相较于这些硬件参数，星芒更大的卖点在于AI。 新机首发搭载HarmonyOS 7 AI先锋版，将系统级AI屏作为核心交互界面，用户解锁手机后，可以直接通过AI提出需求，而不必首先进入传统的App桌面。 华为还为其设计了专属AI形象“小星芒”，支持50余种场景互动，并引入基于使用场景和用户习惯的主动推荐功能。 此外，新机还推出小艺空间、长时任务工作台等功能，尝试让AI从过去的一问一答进一步延伸至长期记忆、持续跟进和主动执行任务。 价格方面，OSTA O1 Pro共推出四个版本。其中，12GB+256GB版本售价5699元，12GB+512GB版本售价6699元，16GB+512GB版本售价7499元，16GB+1TB版本售价8999元。 首发期间，四个版本分别优惠200元，起售价降至5499元。 这一价格也让星芒与外界此前预期的低价走量品牌有所不同。 在存储等零部件成本上涨的背景下，华为并没有选择通过低价打开新品牌的市场，而是以相对高端的硬件配置和新的AI交互体验，吸引愿意尝试新技术的消费者。 华为星芒相关负责人表示，星芒品牌已经在内部酝酿约三年，未来一两年不会被赋予过高的销量和经营目标要求。 相较于短期出货规模，华为现阶段更希望通过星芒建立品牌认知，并验证新的AI技术与产品体验。 不过此次华为仅发布了O1 Pro，并未推出标准版O1。这可能也是为星芒未来进一步丰富产品矩阵、向更低价格区间拓展预留了空间。 从更长的技术周期来看，两次新产品线的诞生也恰好处于两轮技术浪潮之中。 十年前，移动互联网的普及带动了社交、娱乐和移动影像需求的快速增长，智能手机仍有大量市场空间等待开发。nova借助自拍、时尚设计和渠道下沉，抓住了这轮移动互联网红利。 十年后，智能手机的普及红利逐渐消退，生成式AI的兴起却正在为终端市场带来新的想象空间。从被动响应指令到主动理解需求、跨应用执行任务，手机厂商开始尝试以AI重新定义人与终端的交互方式。 十年前，移动互联网创造的需求已经被验证；十年后，AI虽然打开了新的想象空间，但能否真正刺激换机还没有答案。 如何破局AI手机博弈 过去十多年间，智能手机的交互方式并未发生根本变化。用户通过点击不同的App获取服务，应用商店、搜索引擎和各类超级App也由此成为移动互联网的重要流量入口。 但随着Agent技术的发展，这套延续多年的交互方式正在迎来新的变化。 用户可以直接向AI提出需求，由智能体调用不同应用和服务，完成从信息查询到商品购买等一系列任务。 这意味着，AI不仅可能成为刺激换机的新卖点，也可能改变移动互联网原有的服务分发格局。 但技术的演进也正在触动互联网平台原有的利益格局。 手机厂商和AI大厂希望通过系统级智能体直接响应用户需求、调度不同应用，但互联网平台却不愿轻易让出经营多年的流量入口和用户关系。 豆包手机助手此前就遭遇了这一难题。今年10月14日，豆包手机助手公布的拒绝操作应用清单中，微信、淘宝、美团等155款应用明确拒绝其GUI自动化操作，即不允许AI通过识别屏幕、模拟点击等方式代替用户操作应用。 为了协调各方利益，豆包也开始调整技术路线，在新一代产品中更多采用MCP、A2A等协议接入方式，同时推出SAEP协议，让应用开发者自主声明AI操作权限和边界。 这也是整个AI手机行业正在探索的方向。 相比直接模拟用户操作，通过标准化协议连接第三方服务，可以让互联网平台自主决定开放哪些能力，并保留对用户授权、业务流程和交易环节的控制。 包括荣耀、vivo在内的手机厂商，也在积极推进A2A相关合作。 华为同样选择了这条路径。 今年6月，华为发布HarmonyOS 7开发者Beta版本，宣布鸿蒙智能向Agent架构全面演进，并将鸿蒙智能体框架升级至2.0；9月，华为进一步明确了通过Skill及A2A等方式连接第三方智能体的生态路径。 在此次发布的星芒上，华为进一步展示了这套技术体系的应用。 根据现场演示，星芒依托鸿蒙智能体框架HMAF 2.0，能够调用超过2100项系统能力和500余项生态Skills，并通过自然语言交互协调不同服务。 例如，在获得相应授权后，用户可以要求小艺发送微信消息、预约车辆，或整合不同应用中的美食收藏、订单等信息。 在生态合作方面，华为也取得了一定进展，此次合作的生态伙伴包括包括支付宝、小红书、京东、爱奇艺、淘宝、麦当劳、大麦、网易云音乐等。同时微信目前已通过A2A方式与华为进行能力协同，用户可以借助系统助手发送微信消息、发起通话。 华为小艺产品相关负责人透露，目前华为已围绕19个具有一定需求规模的生活服务领域展开合作，基本上每个领域已有一至两家伙伴实现能力打通。 不过，技术协议能够解决服务如何连接的问题，却无法完全消除各方在用户入口、流量分配和商业收益上的分歧。 华为小艺产品相关负责人表示，对于尚未开放的第三方服务，仍需要与生态伙伴逐一沟通，并满足用户授权和平台授权等要求。 未来AI手机的竞争不再只是模型能力和硬件配置的较量，还涉及不同互联网平台之间的商业合作。 鸿蒙的亿级新生意 对华为而言，星芒的意义还不止于验证一种新的手机交互方式。 随着AI开始介入第三方应用的服务分发，手机操作系统也有机会从应用的承载平台，进一步成为连接和调度不同服务的入口。 对于正在建立独立生态的鸿蒙而言，这意味着一次新的竞争机会。 当越来越多消费者通过鸿蒙AI获取第三方服务，开发者便有动力将更多功能接入鸿蒙智能体系；服务能力持续丰富，又有机会进一步提升鸿蒙对消费者的吸引力。 鸿蒙正在跨过这一门槛。第三方数据工具显示，截至11月16日，华为HarmonyOS 5及以上版本累计装机量已突破1亿台。 对互联网平台而言，亿级装机意味着鸿蒙已经拥有不可忽视的潜在用户规模，也为其开放AI服务能力提供了更多商业理由。 而对华为来说，鸿蒙正在从扩大装机规模，进一步走向提高生态活跃度、丰富服务供给的新阶段。 星芒不仅是一次新品牌尝试，也是华为推动鸿蒙从终端规模扩张走向AI服务生态竞争的一次探索。 手机可以通过一次销售获得收入，但操作系统的价值却建立在用户与服务的长期连接之上。从争夺硬件销量，到争夺操作系统的用户和服务生态，华为新品牌背后的生意已经发生变化。 2016年，华为当年第1亿部智能手机提前两个月下线。彼时，手机市场仍在快速扩张，谁能把供应链管好、把产品造好，再通过渠道卖给更多人，谁就有机会在市场竞争中占据上风。 十年后，鸿蒙累计装机量突破1亿台，华为面对的却是另一门生意。 手机可以依靠供应链管理和制造能力不断扩大规模，但AI生态不是一家企业关起门来就能建成的。用户想让AI订餐、叫车、发消息，背后连接的却是不同互联网平台经营多年的生意。 零部件可以采购，应用接口可以通过协议连接，但互联网平台的合作意愿和消费者的使用习惯，却不是华为一家能够决定的。 这也让星芒承担了与当年nova不同的任务。相比再造一款畅销手机，华为更需要验证的是AI能否真正改变用户使用手机的方式，以及鸿蒙能否借此连接起更多第三方服务。 十年前，nova借助移动互联网的红利，帮助华为打开了年轻消费市场；十年后，星芒则试图抓住AI改变终端交互的机会，为鸿蒙争夺更广泛的用户基础。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 三季度热销31万辆，零跑为何只赚4000万元？
articles.summary: 作者 | 周智宇 11月20日晚，零跑汽车交出了季度销量超过31万辆的成绩单，归母净利润却只有约4000万元。去年同期，这个数字是1.5亿元，刚刚过去的二季度则是6亿元。 三季度零跑交付量同比增长78.3%，营收增长63%至317亿元，毛利率却从二季度的12.6%降至10.9%。按财报披露的收入和销售成本计算，零跑一个季度多做了44.1亿元收入，毛利只增加约3000万元，至34.6亿元。 当晚的业绩会上，多位分析师追问毛利率下降的原因。零跑汽车首席财务官李腾飞提到了产品组合变化、原材料涨价和海运费上涨。 零跑三季度卖出的车中，A系列占比提高，B、C、D系列占比相应下降。按李腾飞的解释，A系列每辆车贡献的毛利金额，低于其他几个系列。 原材料涨价也在这一季更明显地体现出来。此前，零跑提前储备了一批原材料，一二季度还能用这些库存抵消部分涨价压力，到了三季度，库存基本耗尽，新的采购价格随之进入成本。李腾飞提到，今年涨价较明显的主要是电芯、内存及芯片、贵金属。 零跑三季度出口6.33万辆，占总交付量的20.4%。这部分业务也没躲过涨价：欧洲、南美长距离航线的海运费上涨，但海外正处于上量阶段，售价无法迅速跟着成本调整。 分析师还追问，海运费上涨如何影响上市公司的毛利，零跑与零跑国际之间又是什么关系。李腾飞解释，零跑向与斯泰兰蒂斯合资成立的零跑国际销售车辆，主要以人民币结算，汇兑损失主要发生在零跑国际。但为了支持海外销量和份额增长，零跑会承担其中一部分负担，包括海运涨价和汇兑损失的影响。 整个汽车行业都在承受成本压力。中国汽车流通协会乘联分会秘书长崔东树披露，今年前三季度，汽车行业收入同比增长2.6%，成本增长3.8%，利润下降23%。 零跑的毛利几乎停留在二季度的水平，研发、销售和行政开支却增加了3.8亿元，合计35.3亿元。其中研发开支14.8亿元，投入和研发人员都在增加；广告宣传、销售及行政人员的增加，也带来了更多开支。财报将归母净利润环比下降归因于费用增加及其他收益减少，公司的经营利润已从二季度的5.4亿元转为亏损3000万元。 零跑仍有资金支撑后续投入。三季度经营现金净流入16.2亿元，期末现金、存款及相关金融资产等合计391.4亿元。海外业务也在继续往前推，10月，西班牙萨拉戈萨工厂已启动B10量产。 当地生产在现有关税条件下能带来一些收益改善，但欧洲的采购和制造费用高于国内。李腾飞坦言，改善幅度“并没有想象中那么大”，这部分制造收益也将体现在零跑国际。 同晚，零跑还公布了一份来自欧宝的1亿欧元合同，为这家斯泰兰蒂斯旗下车企的全新C级SUV提供工程及开发服务。 按李腾飞的介绍，这笔费用包括开发及授权使用费，收入确认从开发阶段开始，一直延续到量产后两至三年。管理层还期待后续零部件供货带来持续收入，不过这部分不在此次协议之内，截至公告披露日，双方尚未签订具有约束力的零部件销售协议。 三季度，零跑还取得了约5亿元碳积分收入，与二季度接近。管理层预计，随着欧洲新能源汽车渗透率提高，2027年的积分单价还会下降。 零跑没有因为利润变薄而收缩：研发还在加码，海外仍要上量，海运和汇率带来的压力，公司也承担了一部分。只是，三季度多卖车带来的毛利，已经不够覆盖新增开支。欧宝的技术合同要分几年兑现，眼前这门卖车生意，还经不起太多成本波动。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
